about: A Python library that turns Excel spreadsheets into Python code and works out their formulas.

prs.title: Weekday formulas with a start-of-week option work
prs.broken: Weekday formulas that count Monday as day one, the usual form in timesheets, crashed instead of giving a result.
prs.changed: The weekday function now accepts every start-of-week option Excel supports, and gives Excel's error for unknown ones.
prs.matters: Timesheet and schedule spreadsheets calculate the same as in Excel.

prs.title: Text numbers with commas, percent or dollar signs are read
prs.broken: Turning text like 1,234.50, 12% or $12.50 into a number gave an error, though Excel reads all three. The error then spread into any total.
prs.changed: Those common formats are now read as numbers the way Excel reads them.
prs.matters: Sheets built on imported or pasted text numbers give the right totals.

prs.title: Numbers joined into text match Excel
prs.broken: Joining a number into text gave long results like Total: 0.30000000000000004, where Excel shows Total: 0.3.
prs.changed: Numbers turned into text are now rounded to 15 digits, as Excel does.
prs.matters: Labels and text built from formulas look the same as in Excel.
